## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta* is the opening discourse of the fourth section of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 100, It 4.1, PTS It 101) [SuttaCentral]. In this discourse, the Buddha depicts himself as a doctor and characterizes his monastic disciples as true heirs in the Dhamma rather than heirs in material things [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, Richard S. Cohen notes that the sutta contains imagery of the Buddha's legitimate or "breast-born" (*aurasa*) son, presenting a parallel formulation to the *Aggañña Sutta* (DN 27), wherein the Buddha rejects Brahmanical claims of spiritual sovereignty from Brahmā's mouth by asserting that his disciples are born of the Dhamma [Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].
Ireland [SuttaCentral; Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].
